title: Young Bankers to Manage AI Agents From Start, Goldman Exec Says
source_used: Bloomberg, relayed by The Straits Times (Bloomberg page blocked: HTTP 403 captcha)
key_facts: Kevin Sneader, who leads Goldman Sachs' business in Asia-Pacific outside Japan, said on 8 Oct 2026 at the Milken Institute Asia Summit in Singapore that new finance hires will be managing AI agents from the time they join.
Sneader said this could make the role of middle managers uncertain: 'We don't quite know what's going to happen to that group.'
Sandra Peterson, operating partner at Clayton, Dubilier & Rice, said the traditional career ladder may not survive.
Chia Der Jiun, managing director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore, said banks will need fewer fresh graduates for analysis and preparatory work.
The panel focused on how roles would be reshaped rather than on mass job losses.
Sneader said AI also makes it easier for young people to start new businesses.
quote_evidence: “When our young folks now start work, they’re managing agents,” Sneader, who leads the Wall Street bank’s business in Asia-Pacific outside Japan, said
“We don’t quite know what’s going to happen to that group.”
why_it_matters_hint: The usual banking career path, where junior staff wait years before managing people, may be reshaped.
